ILSPSD is an Erasmus Mundus master in the international law of security, peace and sustainable development, and its second intake (2027-2029) is now open with the scholarship deadline on 4 January 2027. Self-funded applicants get until 31 March 2027, which makes this one of the more flexible law-focused Mundus options this cycle.

Programme Highlights

  • Law programme bridging security, peacebuilding and sustainability agendas
  • Second intake opens for studies in 2027-2029 with EMJM scholarship funding
  • Two-track deadline: 4 January 2027 for scholarships, 31 March 2027 for self-funded
  • No application fee for the scholarship round

Who Should Apply

Law graduates and students of political science, international relations or development with a strong legal interest. English proficiency documentation follows the consortium's checklist.

Funding and Costs

Erasmus Mundus scholarships cover participation costs plus a monthly allowance; self-funded places remain open until the end of March.

Deadline and How to Apply

Apply on the official ILSPSD platform before 4 January 2027 (23:59 CET) to be considered for the Erasmus Mundus scholarship. Key deadline information: 4 January 2027 (23:59 CET, EMJM scholarship round); self-funded applications until 31 March 2027.

Official Source

  • Official application page (verified link)

About ILSPSD Consortium

The ILSPSD consortium delivers the Erasmus Mundus Joint Master in the International Law of Security, Peace and Sustainable Development, led from France with European partner universities.

Official website: https://master-international-law-erasmusmundus.eu

Contact

Questions about this position, eligibility or the application process should be raised through the contact channel given on the official announcement page (see the Official Link section above). Always quote the position reference in your message so the admissions or HR team can route your enquiry quickly.

Important Notes

  • Application deadline: 4 January 2027 - late or incomplete applications are normally not considered.
  • Listing details were recorded from the official source at the time of publication; always confirm the latest requirements on the official page before applying.
  • Prepare the documents listed in the eligibility and application sections before starting the online form - transcripts, CV and references take the longest to collect.
